guide.title: Install OwneetOS
guide.description: How to install OwneetOS: the requirements, writing the USB stick, starting the PC from it, installing with the controller.
guide.sec.start: Start the PC from the stick
guide.req.cpu.label: Processor
guide.req.firmware.label: Firmware
guide.req.ram.label: Memory
guide.req.graphics.label: Graphics
guide.req.graphics.min: any card (Attention! Without Vulkan the interface goes into “reduced mode”: the Home screen cannot open over a running game, so a short press of Guide does nothing and holding it for 2 seconds closes the game; games that need Vulkan do not start)
guide.req.storage.label: Storage
guide.req.storage.rec: 32 GB + the space your games need
guide.req.stick.label: To install
guide.req.stick.min: a USB stick of 4 GB or more (make sure it’s empty, everything on it will be erased)
guide.req.stick.rec: a USB stick of 4 GB or more (make sure it’s empty, everything on it will be erased)
guide.req.controller.label: Controller
guide.req.uefi.title: Does your PC start in UEFI mode?
guide.req.uefi.1: In Windows, open Start, type `msinfo32` and open **System Information**.
guide.req.uefi.2.uefi: **UEFI**: your PC is suited to run OwneetOS.
guide.req.uefi.2.legacy: **Legacy**: the PC starts the old way. Most PCs from 2012 on can switch to UEFI in their firmware settings: step 4 shows how. A PC that cannot switch is not suited for OwneetOS.
guide.req.erase: Installing erases the whole disk you choose, Windows included. Copy what you want to keep to another disk first.
guide.download.intro: OwneetOS is one file, an **ISO image** of about 2 GB: in step 3 you write it to the USB stick.
guide.download.get.title: Download the file
guide.download.get.1: Press **{get}** at the top right (it comes with the first release). The link takes you to SourceForge, where the download starts.
guide.download.get.2: The downloaded file’s name will be like `owneetos-X.Y.Z-x86_64.iso`, where X, Y and Z are the version number.
guide.download.check.intro: Two checks, for whoever wants them. They are not needed to install OwneetOS.
guide.download.complete.title: Is the file complete?
guide.download.complete.1: From the same page, download also `owneetos-X.Y.Z-x86_64.iso.sha256`, into the same folder as the ISO.
guide.download.complete.2.windows: **Windows**: in that folder, open PowerShell and type `Get-FileHash owneetos-X.Y.Z-x86_64.iso`
guide.download.complete.2.mac: **macOS**: in Terminal, in that folder, type `shasum -a 256 owneetos-X.Y.Z-x86_64.iso`
guide.download.complete.2.linux: **Linux**: in a terminal, in that folder, type `sha256sum -c owneetos-X.Y.Z-x86_64.iso.sha256`: it must say **OK**, and you are done.
guide.download.complete.3: On Windows and macOS, open the `.sha256` file with a text editor: its long code must be the same as the one you got (capital or small letters do not matter). If it is not, download the ISO again.
guide.download.ours.title: Is it really ours?
guide.download.ours.1: You need GnuPG (on Windows, Gpg4win). Download also `owneetos-X.Y.Z-x86_64.iso.sig`, our signature, and [our public key](key), into the same folder.
guide.download.ours.4: It must say **Good signature from “OwneetOS Package Signing”**, with the primary key fingerprint `B3BD F4E3 E477 2D3F 7E86 1A87 8D02 23BC EE51 456E`. A warning that the key “is not certified with a trusted signature” is normal: it only means you have not certified our key yourself; the fingerprint is what counts.
guide.write.intro: Everything on the stick is erased. You can use a free program, such as:
guide.write.etcher: **balenaEtcher** (Windows, macOS, Linux): choose the ISO, choose the stick, then Flash.
guide.write.ventoy: **Ventoy** (Windows, Linux): install it on the stick once, then copy the ISO onto the stick like any file. The stick can keep other ISOs too.
guide.start.intro: Plug the stick in, turn the PC on and press the boot menu key at once, a few times. Choose the USB stick: it shows its name or its maker’s (e.g. “SanDisk” or “USB HDD”). If it appears twice, choose the entry with “UEFI”.
guide.keys.acer.boot: F12 (turn on “F12 Boot Menu” in the firmware first)
guide.start.keys.note: Keys can change between models: the PC often shows them for a moment when it turns on. On laptops you may need Fn with the F key.
guide.start.nokey: **No key works?** From Windows: Settings → System → Recovery → Advanced startup → Restart now, then “Use a device” (the stick), or Troubleshoot → Advanced options → UEFI Firmware Settings. Holding Shift while you choose Restart opens the same menu.
guide.start.firmware: **In the firmware settings**, if the stick does not start or the PC is in Legacy:
guide.start.secureboot: **Secure Boot: off.** Often under Security, Boot or Authentication. Some PCs let you change it only after setting a firmware (supervisor) password.
guide.start.csm: **Legacy or CSM: off**, so the PC starts in UEFI.
guide.start.save: Save and exit, often with F10.
guide.start.anticheat: With Secure Boot off, some Windows games with anti-cheat (e.g. Battlefield 6, Valorant) do not run: they need Secure Boot, and they do not run on OwneetOS.
guide.try.text: The stick starts OwneetOS as it is, without installing: look around, try the controller and the network. Nothing is written on the PC’s disks, and nothing is kept when it turns off.
guide.pic.live-home: Started from the stick: the strip at the top installs it.
guide.install.text: Choose **Install OwneetOS** on Home (or in Settings → System) and follow the screens: no keyboard, no mouse.
guide.pic.installer-disks: Only the PC’s internal disks; Windows and encrypted disks are marked.
guide.pic.installer-warn: Everything on that disk is erased: the console asks you to say you understand.
guide.pic.installer-hold: Hold A for three seconds to start.
guide.install.dualboot: Dual boot is currently not supported.
guide.first.text: The console finds the controller, then asks for the language, the network and the time zone. Without internet choose “Not now”: games on disks and DRM-free games work without it.
guide.pic.first-language: The language: the keyboard follows it.
guide.pic.first-network: The network, for Steam, streaming and updates.
guide.use.guide: **Guide** (the Xbox or PS button) brings you Home from anywhere, games included. While Steam is on screen, hold it for a second.
guide.use.quick: **B on Home** opens the quick menu: power options, and what every button does.
guide.use.updates: **Updates**: the console checks by itself and tells you; you install them in Settings → System when you want. If an update does not work, the console goes back by itself; you can also go back to the previous version, or to any other one, there.
guide.use.disks: **USB disks with games**: play them from the disk, or copy them to the console.
guide.pic.system-update: Settings → System: updates and going back.
guide.help.1.q: The stick is not in the boot menu
guide.help.1.a: Try another USB port (on a desktop, one at the back); turn off Fast Boot and switch Legacy / CSM to UEFI in the firmware settings; as a last resort, write the stick again.
guide.help.2.q: A message about Secure Boot or a security violation
guide.help.2.a: Secure Boot is still on: turn it off in the firmware settings (step 4).
guide.help.3.q: The PC goes straight to Windows
guide.help.3.a: Press the key earlier and more times, or use Windows’ Advanced startup (step 4).
guide.help.4.q: A black screen after the logo
guide.help.4.a: On a desktop with a graphics card, plug the screen into the card, not into the motherboard; then wait a minute.
guide.help.5.q: The installer does not list my disk
guide.help.5.a: It lists only the PC’s internal disks of 32 GB or more: never USB disks.
faq.title: Questions
faq.1.a: Yes: free to use, share and change, under the GPL.
faq.2.q: Do I need a mouse or a keyboard?
faq.2.a: No. Everything works with a controller, from installing it to playing. A mouse and a keyboard still work if you like.
faq.3.a: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and most others, wired or wireless. The first one pairs by itself.
faq.4.a: Most of them, Windows games too. Games whose anti-cheat needs Secure Boot do not.
faq.5.a: No: OwneetOS uses the whole disk. Dual boot is currently not supported.
faq.6.q: Can I watch films and listen to music?
faq.6.a: Yes: your streaming services and your own files, with the controller.
faq.7.q: What if an update goes wrong?
faq.7.a: You can go back to how it was before.
faq.8.a: No. No account, no forced telemetry. Crash reports are sent only if you agree.
faq.9.q: How do I report a problem?
faq.9.a: Open an issue on GitHub: tell us your PC and what happened.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: We collect no data. Here is what that means.
privacy.site.title: This site
privacy.site.text: No cookies, no analytics, no forms, no account. Its fonts and icons come from the site itself: your browser asks nothing of anyone else. Your choice of a light or dark theme stays in your browser only.
privacy.hosting.title: Hosting
privacy.hosting.text: The site is published on GitHub Pages. GitHub may record your address to keep its service safe, as its privacy statement explains.
privacy.os.title: OwneetOS
privacy.os.text: No account and no forced telemetry. A crash report is sent only if you agree.
